messages:
maria: Heads up — saw a p95/p99 regression after the 1.7 canary on Llama-13B with long sequences (>4k). nsys traces show repeated HBM bandwidth spikes aligned with KV cache lookups and a lot of short kernels preempting the big GEMM. Anyone else repro? :eyes:
ajay: Reproduced on dedicated pool. Prefetch miss rate jumps when seq_len > ~3k, and we see eviction waves in the KV allocator. HBM utilization oscillates instead of steady.
devon: Dropped a perfetto link with the timeline: https://perfetto.google.com/trace/viewer?fake=seqwindow (sharing offline). The timeline has dense memcpy bands right before small kernel launches. Looks like a kernel handoff causing memory churn.
maria: nsys command I used to collect the trace:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_seqwindow --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx python -m perf.run_infer --model llm-13b --seq-len 4096 --batch 4
```
Uploaded the raw .qdrep to the s3 bucket.
perf-bot: Deploy-bot: Canary 1.7 flagged by latency-alert (p95+p99 up >20%). Notifying #eng-oncall.
ajay: Kernel selection looks suspicious — the runtime is switching to an int8-prefetch kernel variant for certain sequence windows which forces an alternate KV path that does small memcpy fallbacks. That increases HBM churn. Might be the kernel scoring heuristic mis-evaluating cost for long KV walks.
devon: Also saw batching heuristic amplify it. Microbatching with adaptive packer increases simultaneous KV lookups across threads which causes read storms. Hypothesis: when seq_len is large, microbatch threshold should decrease or enable stronger prefix KV caching.
lucy: I pushed a quick runtime toggle to disable asynchronous prefetch for seq_len > 2048 and started a canary run. Will update results in ~15m.
maria: Quick results — disabling async prefetch brought p95 back near baseline on canary, but throughput dropped ~5%. So it mitigates tail latency but costs throughput. Need smarter decision rule.
ajay: Next steps: run a sweep across seq buckets [512,1024,2048,3072,4096] with nsys sampling HBM counters and collect kernel name histograms. I'll add a script to the perf repo to automate.
devon: I'll add an eval harness (kvcache-stress) to exercise repeated prefixes and emit NVTX ranges: KV_LOOKUP, PREFETCH, MATMUL, KERNEL_DISPATCH. Use flag --batching=adaptive to reproduce production packing.
maria: Filed a short postmortem note and saved traces to s3://redwood-perf/2773331234-seqwindow-traces. Tagging @ajay @devon to attach the nsys .qdrep and perfetto links when available. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
